record.file_problem: The full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study compares extensively tuned Adam with SGD+Momentum on image classification and language modeling, using held-out performance; this is a conceptual test of optimizer-dependent performance.
record.gate_note: The study reports optimizer comparisons and held-out results. Its stated accuracy gaps are used to choose training durations and are not reported as a comparison of training–test gaps across optimizers.
record.test_reason: The study reports its own held-out optimizer comparisons bearing on V4. Figure 12 also compares a convolutional AlexNet with an MLP on Fashion-MNIST, bearing on V3 in an additional image-classification setting.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate but incomplete. The authors conclude that epsilon controls optimizer adaptability; optimal image-classification settings often make Adam behave approximately like SGD+Momentum, whereas language modeling and translation benefit from adaptive updates. Their central contribution is a histogram-based procedure that narrows epsilon search ranges, with experiments suggesting that testing the two bounds can suffice before further learning-rate tuning.
record.recipe_differences: The study tunes Adam's learning rate, ϵ and β2 and compares it with SGD+Momentum; it does not reproduce the cited adaptive-optimizer generalization comparisons or compare training and test performance jointly.
record.method_sensitivity: Task and dataset; optimal ϵ and the effect of β2 vary by task. Fashion-MNIST classification shows similar performance over a wide range of ϵ values.
record.problems: The optimizer comparison values are presented in figures without numeric text values or uncertainty estimates. The paper does not report a direct comparison of training–test gaps across Adam and SGD+Momentum.
record.rows_left_out: No relevant optimizer-comparison results were left out; other model, optimizer, and hyperparameter results do not bear directly on the listed claim versions.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and its coexistence with natural-label generalization.
Width sweeps beyond the width required for zero training error.
The contribution of local connectivity, learned sparse local connections, convolution-derived initialization, and the specified MNIST, CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, and SVHN architecture comparisons.

A controlled optimizer comparison restricted to learning-rate and schedule tuning; equal or better training performance despite worse held-out performance; switching Adam to SGD; and decoupled weight decay.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and recipes for recovering large-batch performance.
Dropout additions, removals, strength, and interactions with dataset size or augmentation.
Magnitude-scaled weight perturbations, their association with generalization gaps, and comparisons with other generalization measures.
Removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

missing.what: Add separate Fashion-MNIST architecture rows: Figure 12 reports maximum test accuracy of 89.2% for the MLP and 93.0% for convolutional AlexNet after 25 epochs. These results bear on V3, although they do not isolate local connectivity as the cause.

record.verdict_notes: This study is not an original source for either tested version. Matching SGD after broader tuning supports a qualification already present in V4; it does not by itself challenge the limited-tuning claim. Test-set maxima across epochs and hyperparameter sweeps are reported without uncertainty estimates, so small numerical advantages should not be treated as established significant differences. The record explicitly declares other optimizer and hyperparameter results excluded; Figures 23–24 nevertheless contain relevant additional held-out optimizer results. The landscape-convexity discussion is speculative and does not test V7.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and generalization on natural labels.
Network width beyond the interpolation threshold.
Language benchmarks beyond Penn TreeBank; broader optimizer families and tuning procedures beyond the study's Adam and SGD+Momentum comparisons; explicit training-performance comparisons.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and other generalization measures.

rows.note: The authors state that Adam in the reported classification settings can closely resemble SGD+Momentum and that this behavior achieves the best performance; no numeric optimizer-to-optimizer comparison is stated in prose.
rows.check: The results bear on V4's broader-tuning qualification, rather than showing an incompletely observed effect. Figures 7 and 14 give tuned Adam accuracies of approximately 87.6% for VGG11, 91.8% for ResNet34, 86.2% for AlexNet, and 92.1% for DenseNet121, matching or exceeding the corresponding SGD+Momentum maxima. Split by architecture. Adam is an optimizer; structural similarity to SGD alone would not establish equivalent held-out performance.

source_check.notes: Checked the exact arXiv:2311.11532v2 source, titled Fine-Tuning Adaptive Stochastic Optimizers: Determining the Optimal Hyperparameter ϵ via Gradient Magnitude Histogram Analysis, by Gustavo Silva and Paul Rodriguez. The displayed maxima are selected across parameter grids and epochs, without displayed uncertainty; they do not isolate a causal effect of expanding the search. Fig. 6b's y-axis is mislabeled Test Accuracy, while its caption identifies lower perplexity as better. The first check's substantive omission is that V4.conflicts[4] calls this evidence qualitative despite readable numeric annotations in the figures; that statement is amended above. No other material omission among the required items found.

statements.correction: The epsilon-tuning study's figures give selected maxima: CIFAR-10 SGD+Momentum versus Adam are VGG11 87.2% versus 87.6%, ResNet34 91.9% versus 92.0%, AlexNet 85.9% versus 86.2%, and DenseNet121 91.8% versus 92.1%. Adam's AlexNet 86.2% is from the beta2/epsilon panel; its learning-rate/epsilon maximum is 85.6%.
statements.problem: The characterization as qualitative is incomplete: the study's figures annotate numeric maxima. For CIFAR-10 ResNet34, Fig. 6a shows SGD+Momentum at 91.9% and Fig. 14 shows an Adam grid maximum of 92.0%.
